chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, and Husayn ibn ibn Uthman, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who died, and one of his inheritors acknowledged a debt on his behalf to a man, he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is binding upon him in his share (of the inheritance).'
ai.seo_question: How is a debt acknowledged by one heir handled in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of individual liability among co-heirs, establishing that an acknowledgment of debt by one heir binds only their specific share rather than the entire estate. This ruling is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for resolving disputes over estate distribution, ensuring that the acknowledging heir bears the burden personally without diminishing the shares of other heirs who did not consent to the debt. It reflects the practical application of 'ithbar' (acceptance) in financial matters within the family structure.
